newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GIANTS BEAT ATLANTA BEHIND TWO BONDS HOME RUNS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GIANTS BEAT ATLANTA BEHIND TWO BONDS HOME RUNS.

text.p: Jeff Kent homered and drove in the go-ahead run with a two-run single in the eighth inning Sunday, lifting the San Francisco to a 5-3 victory over Atlanta that snapped the Braves' road winning streak at six games.

Barry Bonds slugged two homers off Atlanta's John Smoltz, for the 29th two-homer game of his career. Smoltz (6-5) allowed three home runs in a game for the first time since yielding four on June 19, 1994, against Cincinnati.
"Smoltz is always ahead of you and he has that great split-finger pitch," Bonds said. "If you're not aggressive from the beginning, he's going to slam the door."

"There are some games you don't feel you should have lost and this is one of them," Smoltz said. "I had some opportunities to make some pitches in the eighth inning, but I hung two sliders and that was the ballgame."

San Francisco's Shawn Estes, who won eight of his first 10 decisions, struck out six, but allowed three runs and nine hits. He had yielded three runs over 21 innings in his previous three starts, including a 4-2 win at Atlanta.
Giants reliever Jim Poole (3-1) retired the only batter he faced in the eighth to pick up the win.

Rod Beck retired the side in order in the ninth for his 19th save in 21 opportunities. The 19 saves tied him with Mariano Rivera of the New York Yankees and Baltimore's Randy Myers for the major league lead.
In Montreal, Mike Lansing and F.P. Santangelo hit back-to-back RBI doubles with one out in the ninth inning to rally the Montreal Expos to a 5-4 victory over the Chicago Cubs.

Ryan McGuire led off the ninth with an infield single off closer Terry Adams (0-3) for the Expos. One out later, Santangelo slugged an RBI double to tie the game. Lansing's double to left scored Santangelo with the winning run.

Anthony Telford (2-0) retired all six batters he faced to notch the win for the Expos. Montreal starter Pedro Martinez did not get the decision, but he struck out the side in both the first and fourth innings while establishing a career-high with 13 strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings.
In Pittsburgh, Curt Schilling struck out 11 batters over eight innings and Ruben Amaro's RBI single capped a three-run sixth that lifted the Philadelphia Phillies over the Pittsburgh Pirates, 3-2.
Schilling (8-5) allowed both runs, five hits and two walks. Ricky Bottalico recorded his 13th save.
Steve Cooke (7-7) allowed three runs, seven hits and two walks with three strikeouts in six innings.
In Los Angeles, Delino DeShields homered and drove in three runs and Matt Morris allowed three runs over six innings, carrying the St. Louis Cardinals to a 9-3 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Morris (4-3) won his third straight despite giving up 11 hits.
Pedro Astacio (3-5) allowed five runs and nine hits over four innings and lost for the fifth time in six starts.
In San Diego, Darryl Kile tossed a five-hitter for his second shutout of the year and every Houston starter had a hit as the Astros routed the San Diego Padres, 9-0.

Kile (7-2) walked one and struck out two for his sixth straight victory and fourth career shutout. The right-hander has pitched at least seven innings in 13 of 14 starts this season. Sean Berry paced the Astros with three hits and two runs scored, while Kile was the only starter not to score.
The Padres did not advance a runner to third all game.

In Denver, John Burke allowed two runs and five hits over six innings and Andres Galarraga drove in two runs to lead the Colorado Rockies to a 7-2 victory over the Florida Marlins in the first game of a day-night doubleheader.
Jerry Dipoto pitched three hitless innings in reliefe of Burke (2-1), to notch his second save.
Al Leiter (5-4), who was reached for seven runs and 11 hits while walking two and striking out five over five innings, took the loss after posting victories in his last two starts.
In the nightcap, the Marlins rolled to a 9-1 win in a rain shortened game called after seven innings. Alex Fernandez (6-6) struck out 10 and gave up just five hits.
Moises Alou had three hits and four RBI to lead the Marlins. Alou drove in two runs in the third and had RBI singles in the first and seventh.
In Cincinnati, the game between the New York Mets and Cincinnati Reds was postponed due to rain. It will be made up on Monday.
